top_cluster.headline: Florida, Alaska, and Wyoming held primary elections in which Democratic socialist Angie Nixon upset establishment favorite Alex Vindman for the Florida Senate nomination, scandal-plagued GOP Rep. Cory Mills lost his House primary, and Trump-endorsed candidates split results — winning in Florida's governor race but losing Wyoming's governor primary.
top_cluster.left_framing: Emphasizes accountability and hypocrisy narratives — Mills' loss as scandal comeuppance, Trump's mail-ballot use contradicting his fraud claims, Ossoff's 'draft-dodging crook' attack — and celebrates Nixon's DSA-backed win as a historic grassroots breakthrough against establishment money, while casting Trump's foreign policy moves (South Korea drawdown, Oman threats) as erratic and alliance-straining.
top_cluster.center_framing: Largely procedural and horse-race oriented — reporting who won/advanced in Florida, Alaska, and Wyoming races with minimal ideological framing — though The Hill and Politico both note a pattern of Trump-endorsed candidates (Degenfelder, Webster's pick) losing primaries as a notable storyline.
top_cluster.right_framing: Frames results through Trump's continued dominance over the GOP (Donalds, Hageman, Gray wins) and treats Democratic-side news as evidence of party dysfunction — Nixon's win exposing Vindman's 'TDS-addled' hypocrisy and wasted establishment money — while covering Alaska's jungle primary as an orderly process threatened by 'far-left meddling,' and framing Trump's Canada tariffs as justified leverage.
top_cluster.left_omissions: Left coverage largely omits or downplays Trump-aligned wins as validation of his influence (e.g., Donalds', Hageman's, Gray's victories) and doesn't cover the 'far-left meddling' framing of Alaska's primary or the vote-splitting Dan Sullivan theory that right-leaning/libertarian outlets raised.
top_cluster.right_omissions: Right coverage largely omits the mail-voting hypocrisy story, the Ossoff-Harp/plane-switch security scrutiny story, and does not frame Barlow's or Vindman's-opponent's wins as signs of any erosion in Trump's or the GOP's political dominance, instead isolating each result as a discrete outcome.

blindspot_narrative: The left is systematically avoiding stories where Republican local wins or cultural-conservative arguments stand on their own (California special election, crime-decline data, Ukraine corruption critique) while amplifying every available thread of alleged administration overreach (FCC, DOJ, ICE, DOD). The right is systematically avoiding stories that put Trump or his administration in legal or ethical jeopardy (Ballroom SCOTUS fight, Bessent assassination-plot sentencing, election-denier candidates) while leaning into culture-war and socialism-threat framing. Both patterns point to curation around narrative reinforcement rather than shared-fact reporting — neither side is being confronted with inconvenient developments on its own side today.
